# Results — Study 693 (Tasuki Gap)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
gap in the trend, then a small candle of the opposite color that pulls back but does
NOT close the gap, then the trend resumes** — tested as a trend-**signed** event study
(long on an upside tasuki, short on a downside tasuki) on a fixed **30-name liquid US
large-cap + SPY** basket. For every confirming bar we enter the next open (one lag),
hold 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 trading days in the predicted trend direction, and measure the
signed return against the basket's own **direction-matched unconditional** base rate
(not against zero — see the note below) and against a mix-matched coin-flip placebo.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; 2026-07 is dropped as
partial). Fingerprints `8af479f8c79c` (quantlab `data_stamp` on the 30-name close panel)
/ `aa438a4d53ea` (basket sha1, `data.fingerprint`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` — 30 long-listed liquid US large-caps + **SPY** (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (last complete calendar month; run 2026-07-10) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**21.5** years; **162,180** total bars, 5,406 rows/name) |
| Fingerprints | `8af479f8c79c` (quantlab `data_stamp`, 30-name close panel) / `aa438a4d53ea` (`data.fingerprint`, sha1 of the same closes) |
| Detector | textbook tasuki gap on bars (t−2, t−1, t): **upside** — two same-color WHITE bodies gapping up (body-level gap, default), then a BLACK body that opens inside bar t−1's body and closes back inside the gap without filling it; **downside** — the exact mirror (two BLACK bodies gapping down, a WHITE pullback body that doesn't fill the gap). Strict full-range-gap + prior-trend-context variants for the myth-check |
| Timing / costs | confirm at close of t; enter the **next open** (one lag); hold 1/5/10/20 days, signed **toward the predicted trend direction** (+1 × forward move on an upside tasuki = long, −1 × forward move on a downside tasuki = short); **5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) on every event + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short (downside) leg only |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names that are *still
> trading* in 2026. A fixed surviving-names panel skews slightly **toward** finding a
> working bullish-continuation signal (it excludes names whose "resumed uptrend" never
> came because they later delisted) and, symmetrically, slightly **against** finding a
> working bearish-continuation signal on the downside leg (survivors, by construction,
> didn't keep falling forever). Both directions are reported separately below so this
> asymmetry is visible rather than averaged away.

## The certifying comparison — why Welch-vs-base, not a plain t-vs-zero

The basket carries the market's ordinary positive drift, so a naive one-sample *t* of
the trend-signed return against **zero** is contaminated: an upside (long) event would
look "significant" merely from riding the market's up-drift, with or without any tasuki
gap, and a downside (short) event would look artificially *worse* fighting that same
drift. The fair test signs the **basket's own unconditional forward-return pool** to
match each event's direction (long events vs the plain pool, short events vs its
negation) and runs a Welch *t* against that direction-matched pool — beating "just
trading the basket's own drift, long or short" is the bar an actual continuation edge
has to clear. Both the plain HAC-vs-zero and the decisive Welch-vs-base numbers are
reported below.

## The headline — trend-signed forward return after a tasuki gap

| horizon | n (up/dn) | signed mean | base (matched) | hit-rate (Wilson 95%) | base hit-rate | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0, informational) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 1,277 (656/621)  | **+0.007%** | +0.000% | 48% [45.7%, 51.2%] | 50% | **+0.15** | +0.15 | 0.429 |
| 5-day  | 1,273 (655/618)  | **−0.259%** | +0.000% | 48% [44.9%, 50.4%] | 50% | **−2.33** | −2.40 | 0.995 |
| 10-day | 1,269 (652/617)  | **−0.189%** | +0.000% | 49% [46.4%, 51.9%] | 50% | **−1.29** | −1.38 | 0.924 |
| 20-day | 1,267 (651/616)  | **−0.011%** | +0.000% | 50% [47.6%, 53.1%] | 50% | **−0.05** | −0.06 | 0.585 |

Read it carefully: the pattern is common (≈1,270 confirmed events, a near-even 51/49
up/down split) but the trend-signed return is **flat at 1 day, negative at 5 and 10
days, and flat again at 20**. Only the 5-day mark clears |*t*| ≥ 2 — and it clears it on
the **wrong side**: *t* = −2.33 means the pattern's own predicted direction did *worse*
than the basket's unconditional drift, not better. Hit rates track (or trail) the base
hit rate at every horizon. The mix-matched coin placebo puts the 5-day observation at
*p* = 0.995 — i.e. **99.5% of random draws in the same long/short mix beat the
observed mean** — the opposite of what a genuine continuation edge would show.

### Split by direction — the up leg and the down leg separately

| horizon | up-only mean | up Welch *t* (n) | down-only mean | down Welch *t* (n) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.000% | −0.50 (656) | +0.014% | +0.61 (621) |
| 5-day  | +0.150% | −0.72 (655) | −0.692% | **−2.58** (618) |
| 10-day | +0.518% | −0.05 (652) | −0.935% | **−1.98** (617) |
| 20-day | +1.235% | +0.50 (651) | −1.328% | −0.80 (616) |

The **upside** (bullish-continuation) tasuki never clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in *either*
direction at any horizon — its point estimate is small and sign-flips across horizons.
The **downside** (bearish-continuation) tasuki is the leg carrying the headline's dip:
at 5 and 10 days its signed-short return is *negative* at *t* = −2.58 / −1.98 — i.e.
shorting after a downside tasuki tends to lose money relative to shorting the basket
unconditionally, a mild **reversal**, not the claimed continuation. Neither leg supports
the folklore; if anything the down leg leans the opposite way, and it doesn't survive
Bonferroni below.

## The continuation timer — cost sweep

Every event pays a fresh round trip: **5 / 10 bps one-way × 2**; downside (short)
events additionally pay **50 bps/yr** borrow over the hold.

| horizon | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +0.007% | **−0.094%** | −0.194% |
| 5-day  | −0.259% | **−0.364%** | −0.464% |
| 10-day | −0.189% | **−0.298%** | −0.398% |
| 20-day | −0.011% | **−0.131%** | −0.231% |

There is no horizon where the trend-signed trade clears zero gross, let alone its own
costs, let alone the direction-matched base it should be beating. Nothing under the
signal to charge costs against.

## Bonferroni across the basket — no single name carries it either

Per-ticker pooled (up+down) Welch *t* (event sample vs that ticker's **own**
direction-matched unconditional pool) at the 5-day horizon, for the 30 tickers with
≥ 6 events. With **k = 30** simultaneous tests the two-sided Bonferroni bar is
**|t| ≥ 3.14** (vs the usual 1.96):

| ticker | n | mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| MRK  | 49 | −1.683% | −2.15 |
| CSCO | 44 | −0.843% | −1.89 |
| SPY  | 50 | −0.504% | −1.73 |

**0 / 30 tickers clear the corrected bar.** Even the loudest name in the basket (MRK,
and again the *wrong* sign for a continuation story) doesn't survive the
multiple-testing correction. No single name is quietly carrying the pattern.

## Myth check #1 — the strict true-range gap

Tighten the rule to the purist's gap (bar1's entire wick range clears bar0's, no overlap
at all, not even in the wicks). If the lore hid in a "cleaner" gap, this should surface
a real continuation edge. It doesn't (and events are roughly a third as common):

| horizon | n (up/dn) | mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 472 (244/228) | −0.007% | −0.09 | −0.09 | 0.548 | −0.108% |
| 5-day  | 469 (243/226) | −0.231% | −1.20 | −1.24 | 0.927 | −0.335% |
| 10-day | 467 (241/226) | −0.186% | −0.69 | −0.65 | 0.812 | −0.296% |
| 20-day | 467 (241/226) | +0.271% | +0.68 | +0.68 | 0.233 | +0.151% |

## Myth check #2 — only patterns that continue a genuine prior trend

A tasuki gap is *supposed* to continue an established move, not just any two-candle
gap-and-pullback. Restrict to patterns whose prior trend (close at t−3 vs 10 sessions
earlier) actually agrees with the predicted direction — a genuine continuation setup,
not a reversal wearing the shape. Still nothing supportive — if anything, worse:

| horizon | n (up/dn) | mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 616 (349/267) | +0.092% | +1.31 | +1.45 | 0.057 | −0.009% |
| 5-day  | 614 (348/266) | −0.358% | **−2.03** | −2.03 | 0.998 | −0.462% |
| 10-day | 612 (347/265) | −0.502% | **−2.36** | −2.34 | 0.998 | −0.611% |
| 20-day | 612 (347/265) | −0.435% | −1.51 | −1.54 | 0.979 | −0.552% |

Restricting to "genuine trend" patterns makes the 5- and 10-day dip *more* pronounced,
not less — the opposite of what the folklore predicts, and still nowhere near a
tradable edge once costs are charged.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic OHLCV panel with an overnight-gap component and a mild embedded drift (so
the raw material for the pattern — genuine same-color gap pairs followed by an
opposite-color pullback — actually occurs), with a TUNABLE planted post-pattern
continuation; no network. The certifying statistic is Welch *t* vs the direction-matched
unconditional base (the same drift-neutral comparison used on the real tape).

| world | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0) | hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.41** (sd 1.12), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | — | — |
| null (edge = 0, seed 693) | −0.76 | −0.82 | 50% |
| planted edge = +0.012/day (seed 693) | **+8.06** | +8.60 | 65% |
| planted edge = +0.020/day (seed 693) | **+13.85** | +14.85 | 72% |

The null fires in 1 of 20 independent seeds at the 2-sigma bar — right at the ~5%
nominal false-positive rate of a two-sided two-sigma test, not a systematic bias — and a
planted continuation of 1.2%/day or 2.0%/day lights the detector up cleanly
(*t* = 8.1 and 13.9). The harness *would* catch a real tasuki continuation if one
existed, so the real tape's failure to certify is a genuine **absence** of signal, not a
broken detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The certifying, direction-matched comparison (Welch *t* vs the
  matched unconditional base) never certifies a continuation at any horizon
  (+0.15 / −2.33 / −1.29 / −0.05 for 1/5/10/20 days) — the one horizon that clears
  |*t*| ≥ 2 (5-day) does so on the **wrong side** (the pattern underperforms the base,
  a mild reversal, not a continuation), driven by the downside (short) leg specifically
  (*t* = −2.58 at 5 days). The mix-matched placebo places the 5-day observation at
  *p* = 0.995 — worse than 99.5% of random draws in the same mix. **0 of 30 tickers**
  survive a Bonferroni correction individually. Neither the strict full-range gap nor a
  genuine prior-trend-context filter rescues it — the trend-context filter makes the
  5/10-day dip *more* pronounced. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross is flat-to-negative at every horizon (+0.007% to
  −0.259%) and net of a round-trip cost + short borrow it is negative everywhere
  (−0.094% to −0.464% across the 5/10-bps sweep). There is no edge to charge costs against.
- **"Predicts continuation?" — BUSTED.** The claim that a gap plus an incomplete
  pullback signals the trend has enough force left to resume does not survive contact
  with 21.5 years of tape, once measured fairly against what the same basket does
  unconditionally. If anything, the downside leg shows a faint, non-Bonferroni-robust
  *reversal* tendency at intermediate horizons — the opposite of the textbook claim.
